column1: # Editor's blind re-rulings of the 15 tightest Couples/Golden boundary cases.
# Editor was sent the blind client file (no true_section / model_pred) -> valid self-consistency test.
# C = For Couples, G = For Golden Age Readers.
#   Held LOOSELY: n=15, wide CI (~55-93%). The "directional Couples->Golden drift" read on the
#   3 disagreements (#4/#10/#15) was DROPPED -- n=3 is noise, not signal.
#   Durable takeaway: the C/G boundary is genuinely fuzzy -> abstention on this pair is load-bearing.
#   The ambiguity is QUANTIFIED by the model's probability margin (|p_couples - p_golden|); small
#   margin = hard = flex candidate. Threshold on margin = the easy/medium/hard split.
# FLEX-FLAG design (parked, spans R7->R6): low-margin C/G events get a "flex" flag emitted by R7;
#   R6/allocator resolves them by dropping the card into whichever section is short that week
#   (scarcity resolves the ambiguity for free). R7 EMITS the flag, R6 CONSUMES it -- keep layers clean.
#   Two separate dials: margin tunes flex VOLUME; editor-150 checks flex QUALITY (true dual-fit vs
#   model-just-confused). Extends the existing flex-segment idea (Decision_Log -- verify entry).
#   Margin calibration is a BUILD-TIME check (scope's calibration tripwire), not a design-now item.
